text:
ConocoPhillips likely fell today on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict and shifting political winds. Crude oil prices dropped for a second consecutive day as the U.S. and Iranian presidents signaled openness to negotiation, easing immediate supply concerns that had been supporting higher prices. A Democratic Congress, now poised to take control, is also seen as more favorable to renewable energy development and potentially less supportive of traditional oil expansion — a structural headwind for large oil producers.

The price action reflects a broader market repricing: geopolitical risk premiums built into oil are unwinding, and the political shift away from Republican control removes a traditionally pro-fossil-fuel voice in Congress. Even with U.S. crude still above $103 per barrel, the trajectory matters more to equity investors than the absolute level.
